recipes.name: Guinness Bread
ingredients_raw: 1 cup regular rolled oats, plus additional
1 (12 fluid ounce) can or bottle Guinness® beer

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Grease an 8x8-inch baking pan.

Mix oats, flour, sugar, baking soda, baking powder, and salt together in a bowl. Stir butter, vanilla, buttermilk, and Guinness together in a separate large bowl. Pour flour mixture into beer mixture, and gently stir until well combined. Pour batter into the prepared baking pan, and sprinkle with additional oats if desired.

Bake in preheated oven for 30 minutes, then turn the temperature down to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C), and bake for an additional 30 minutes. Turn the oven off, open the door, and allow to cool for 30 minutes in the oven before turning out onto a wire rack.

raw_recipe.headline: Guinness Bread
raw_recipe.description: This Guinness beer bread made with buttermilk and Irish stout is an incredibly flavorful and hearty brown soda bread that's great with soup.

review.reviewBody: This was super! ....moist, flavorful, hearty, and relatively healthy. First of all, I did not use Guinness. I had a Smithwick's on hand so I had to make the best of it. I did not have buttermilk so I used 1 Tbsp of lemon juice mixed with 1c milk and let it sit for 5 min. I used splenda brown sugar mix, light butter, and baked it in an 8x6 pan for ten minutes less than stated. It was perfect and just may have to replace my go-to beer bread recipe from this site (whole wheat beer bread). Loved this this one had oats. Also, I wasn't expecting it to be as sweet as it was and may decrease the sugar next time. Although my sweet tooth can't complain. Thank you for the recipe!

I used Raz-ber-rita as the ale in this bread that I spread into a 9"x13" pan. The baking time was 35 minutes in a 350 oven. I made frosting using butter, Raz-ber-rita,and powdered sugar. Fantastic recipe! I think this will be a snack rather than a coffee cake type of bread!

This came out perfect and was really easy to make. Not as sweet as banana bread, but with a little sweetness to be perfect eaten plain. I used Leinenkugel Snowdrift Vanilla Porter instead of Guinness, which still gave it a great dark finish. I used a round cake pan, and within the first ten minutes in the oven it rose up about a half inch over the top of the pan. But it was fine and nothing spilled over. After cooling, it retreated back into the pan.

Great recipe! I didn't have any buttermilk, so I used Greek yogurt. I only had half a cup of plain, so I used that and half a cup of vanilla yogurt. I cut back the added vanilla to 1 teaspoon. I used a loaf pan and cooked it for 30 minutes at 375, then 40 minutes at 350. I let it cool in the oven for 30 minutes. The bread is dense but not dry. The exterior has a pleasing light crunch. There's just a faint taste of the bitter Guinness. A little honey butter on a warmed slice puts it over the top. It's gotta be healthy with all that whole wheat flour, oatmeal and yogurt, right? :)

I love this recipe. I’ve made it many times and it’s a staple with every St. Patrick’s Day meal. This year I doubled the recipe and made Guinness biscuits instead of loaves. Followed the recipe exact other than doubling it. Set the oven for 400 degrees, poured an ice-cream scoop of batter in each greased muffin tin and baked for 13 minutes. They came out beautifully!
Great, easy, forgiving. Changes, rye flour, pumpkin seed, Bushmills doubled for vanilla, half & half plus two tablespoons yogurt for buttermilk I dare you! House favorite ❤️

Made this and its very good and very easy. Only change was to use a single loaf pan, baked at 400 for 30 minutes then turned the oven down to 350 for 25 minutes. Turned out perfectly. It's a total keeper!

I didn't have wheat flour, so I used all-purpose. I also substituted light vanilla soy milk and vinegar for the buttermilk. I used Irish steel cut oats and Smart Sense spread instead of butter. I cooked it at 425 F for 15 minutes, then 400 F for 15 minutes, then let it sit in the oven. Despite all these changes, it turned out very well. I think it would have been fine cooking as the recipe states, but I like how it came out--crispy on the outside and tender and chewy on the inside. The flavors were a unique treat for my tongue, and I found myself chewing slowly and really focusing on what I was tasting. I will definitely make this again! Very easy, tasty, and pretty!

The batter was much runnier than I was expecting, even with an 11.2 oz Guinness rather than 12 oz. I tried to put it in a loaf pan, but it was all the way to the top, so I located a 6” x 8” pan and used that. It looked like it was possibly burning on the top—certainly very dark—so I only left it in the oven for 15 min after I turned it down to 400. Most beer bread recipes have you bake at 350, so I might bake it 25 degrees lower next time. Might also add a little bit more flour and use two loaf pans instead. I certainly plan on making it again. It’s very good. The sweetness isn’t overwhelming and goes well with the dark beer flavor. It’s closer in texture to a moist fruit bread rather than most of the beer bread I’ve made in the past. It’s going to make great toast at breakfast time.

Really good! Instead of melted butter, I cut 1/2 cup cold butter into the flour mixture and baked in a loaf pan 35 minutes at 375, then 40 minutes at 325. Turned oven off and let set with oven door open another 35 minutes. Wonderful!

The temp and cooking time seemed off when I started at 425. It started to cook really fast on too. I decided to turn down to 400 after 10 mins. Then at the 30 min mark it was done. I bake a lot and think the temp needs to be 350 and bake 40-45 min. Very good bread. It is more of a quick soft bread like banana bread.
I found this recipe a couple of years ago. I made it as directed, and cooked it in a loaf pan. It was a huge hit with the family and I have been making it every year since.

Easy recipe that turned out delicious! I had to use a round 2 quart dish and it worked well. I had to cut cooking time to 20 minutes at 425 and 20 at 400 then we put it in the microwave for 30 minutes instead of leaving in the oven as we thought it would get over done. It was very moist and has great flavor.
This recipe is awful, I followed the directions exactly except it was already overdone after the first 30 minutes. Too dry to even eat!
This recipe is easy and makes the most delicious bread! It's so hearty and different from traditional soda bread which we love. My family couldn't get enough.
Superb - I tried Guinness bread during a recent trip to Dublin and had been craving it ever since. Your recipe is spot on - dare I say it better than the original from Ireland :)

A coworker's wife made Guinness bread and it was quite nice so I decided to give this a shot. Initially, we tried it during covid and I had left over wheat flour. Fast forward to 2024, and there was still a can of Guinness at the back of the fridge! The edges and top is crispy, and the interior has a good chew, with a slight earthy or fermented aroma of the Guinness. I don't like or drink beer but this loaf is intriguing. Certainly good for snacking. I subbed molasses and sorghum for brown sugar to reduce all the bottles in my cupboard and quite liked the low level of sweetness. Probably make this again for beer bros. Sadly, this is not gluten free but a lovely loaf. Thank you!!
Only change I made was an addition of blonde raisins, handful! I have made this several times & it remains a keeper
I make this recipe all the time, it always turns out moist and delicious
Excellent. Not too crumby not too moist just the right stout taste. Big hit
